
# Blue Meridian

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-070636.png](data:image/png;base64,)

Under the OISNT category which basically stands for (Open Source Intelligence) this was the third challenge among the three.

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-071049.png](data:image/png;base64,)

To solve this challenge I had to analyse `field-notes.zip` dump which was provided upon visiting the link to the page `http://54.72.82.22:8500`
After unziping the .Zip archive I  got six files each showning how to achieve the goal and retrieve the flag:

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-093157.png](data:image/png;base64,)

Some of the files contained a huge chunk amount of metadatadata that I could not just `cat` and view from the terminal so I opened the directory on vscode to view all the files simultaneously to form the link between them.

For starters I opened the `submission.txt` file since I wanted to know what I am uo against and how I will achieve it:
Basically the file contained the format on how I am suppose to submit the receipt to retrieve the flag from the server

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-094429.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`Receipt format: SHA256(voyage_ref|station_ref|UTC_time), lowercase hex. UTC_time uses HH:MMZ.
So this was the format on how I was suppose to submit the receipt
From here I understood the goal was to retrieve three values from the metadata acquired from the archive:
1. Get `voyage_ref`
2. Get `station_ref`
3. Get `UTC_time` 

Before I could analyze the metadata on voyages I went through the `pier-note.txt` to find out what it really contained:

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-095139.png](data:image/png;base64,)

Keep in mind the gauge number `219cm` it came in hand later on when solving this challenge:

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-100111.png](data:image/png;base64,)

 From the camera metadata I got my first value:The UTC_time which was just sitting there in plain text
From the screenshot we can see the `utc_offset` is set to `+02:00` and the local timee we are give as `21:00`
To get the UTC_TIME we subtract two hours which the offset given to get `19:00`
So from here I already have `UTC_time` - __19:00__ 

From here I went forward to analyse the `tide-station.csv`  metadata where I found the next value:
Now from this file the tide was measured in __cm__ and every value against the station `ref number ` 
From the pier-note.Text file we already realized the gauge had a value __219 cm__ 

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-101403.png](data:image/png;base64,)

Now only one value is roaming to solve the puzzle:
`UTC_time` - __19:00__
`station_ref` - __5255073ff2__

I continued now to the voyages metadata to get the final value to this puzzle:
Now to get the final value I had to skim through the whole metadata of different voyages and cross-checking the ref number agins the station ref number and the tide value since the metadata was in the format:

`{"ref": "<ref_number>", "vessel": "<vessel_number>, "station": "<station_re_number>", "utc_hour": HH, "tide_cm": <number_cm>, "bearing": <bearing_number>}`

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-102919.png](data:image/png;base64,)

When solving this puzzle I had to  be extra cautious since the author intentionally place a decoy voyage with the same station number as the one  I was hunting for:

![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-104933.png](data:image/png;base64,)

`voyage_ref` - __d0b36031a079e290__ 
`UTC_time` - __19:00__
`station_ref` - __5255073ff2__

Now to finally solve the puzzle I had to honor the authors format before submitting receipt to the server:
`Receipt format: SHA256(voyage_ref|station_ref|UTC_time), lowercase hex. UTC_time uses HH:MMZ

__SHA256(d0b36031a079e290|5255073ff2|19:00Z)__
So the __Z__ at the end of the time is referred to as __Zulu time__ which basically means that the time is already in __UTC__ time format

The value above is now what I was to hash it using the sha256 function to compute the SHA-256 digest of the input:
![PwnZone-CTF-2026/OSINT/Blue Meridian 20261004-110400.png](data:image/png;base64,)

```
echo -n "d0b36031a079e290|5255073ff2|19:00Z" | sha256sum
```

The 64 hex string we computed is now the value we send to the server to retrieve the flag in the form of: __Safctf{this_is_not_the_flag_retrived}__
